2.text: As to patterns formed of square pieces of skin, the Chukchee women

3.text: make but very few, using them to decorate caps, hoods, leg-openings of trousers,

4.text: the upper edges of boots, ear-laps (see Fig. 183, a), etc. Among the square

5.text: pieces of skin they may insert a small bit of red flannel. The whole work

6.text: is crude and irregular. The patterns made by the Koryak women are much

7.text: more elaborate. The collections include a coat of Koryak make, with a large

8.text: band around the skirt formed of several thousand small squares sewed together

10.text: Embroidering with beads is practised very little. Pouches for tobacco

11.text: and strike-a-lights are often adorned with beads, but most of these pouches

12.text: are bought either from Lamut or from Alaskan Eskimo. I found among the

13.text: Reindeer Chukchee a pouch which undoubtedly came from the Athapascan

14.text: Indians. Chukchee work of this kind is a mere imitation of foreign patterns.
